result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Use an exclusive merge for alternative paths; it does not wait for inactive alternatives.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.

result.rule: When the description states that a process can begin through alternative channels before continuing through a shared flow: Model each channel as a separate branch and merge the branches with an exclusive gateway before the shared flow.
When the description states that an action has mutually exclusive alternatives for how or where it is carried out: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway and a separate task for each alternative.
When the description states that an additional activity may be performed.: Model that activity on an optional branch, preserving its connection to the subsequent flow.

When the description presents multiple distinct activities as optional alternatives: Model each activity separately on an appropriate branch, rather than combining the alternatives into one activity, and preserve their connection to the subsequent flow.
